name: Hosanna-Tabor Evangelical Lutheran Church and School v. EEOC
summary: The Supreme Court unanimously held that the First Amendment's religion clauses bar employment discrimination suits brought against religious organizations by their 'ministers,' broadly defined as employees who perform important religious functions.
significance: This is the landmark case establishing the 'ministerial exception,' which bars employment discrimination suits brought by employees who perform religious functions, and is central to the Missionaries' argument that the First Amendment protects their personnel decision.
